_note: Edge-primitive fixture. Every run below is either a RAILING (polyline, height, post pitch, rail count) or a SWEEP (a cross-section extruded along an arbitrary 3D polyline). Nothing here names a vessel: a path plus a profile name is the whole vocabulary, and the same two emitters draw a passenger-ferry guardrail, a bulwark cap, a rubbing strake, a waterline stripe and a hydraulic pipe run. Paths are ship-local metres, bow is -Z, one unit is one metre and a player is 1.8. A 'path_source' resolves to a polyline derived from HullStations at load time instead of being written out by hand - that is how the sheer curve, which HullStations has derived per hull all along and nothing has ever drawn, enters the world.

trawler_ref._note: Proportions of a small working hull. The catalog's own hull_28x10 numbers, resolved through HullFormProfile so the sheer rise is DERIVED (freeboard 2.8 m x fine_entry bow_keel_rise 0.32 = 0.896 m forward) and not written down here as a magic number.

runs._note: The gap this fixture exists to close: an open upper deck a person walks off. Path is the deck edge inset 0.15 m, three sides of a 12.5 x 16.85 m open deck = 46.2 m of run. Height 1.1 m against a 1.8 m figure; three courses over the clear height put every opening at 0.333 m, inside the 0.38 m limit; a 0.1 m toe board stops a dropped tool going over the side.
Same primitive, closed loop, no toe board, four courses - a walkway rail round a machinery casing. Present to prove the closed-loop path and the rail-count parameter carry no special cases.

THE SHEER LINE. A 0.22 x 0.06 m cap band swept along the hull's own deck-edge loop, with Y taken from HullStations.sheer_cap_y_at plus a 0.95 m bulwark. On a real boat the sheer line IS the bulwark cap, and this is the first thing in the project to draw it. The 0.95 m offset is the bulwark's own height: sheer_cap_y_at is deck_y + rise, and rise is ZERO amidships, so a cap swept straight along it would lie in the deck plate (which fills deck_y..deck_y+0.1) and under the build plane at deck_y+0.12. The curve is HullStations'; the bulwark height is the caller's, which is exactly the split STATE.md describes.

Same emitter, different rect: a proud half-round on the topsides 0.2 m below the deck edge, parallel to the sheer. The half-beam is read at the strake's own height, so it hugs the narrower section it actually sits on instead of standing off a flared topside.

Paint, not moulding, and the reason follow_sheer exists: a boot top is parallel to the WATERLINE. Held at a constant Y (deck_y - 2.75) while the cap above it curves. 12 mm proud so it never planes against the shell.

An ARBITRARY 3D polyline - it turns in plan AND climbs in elevation, which a deck-edge height curve could not express. Octagonal section from two rolled rects. This is the generalisation earning its keep: the pipe run is the sheer band with a different cross-section and no code in common beyond the emitter.
Three rolled rects make a D-section lobe. Hung on a straight run along a quay face or a workboat's rail - no hull needed, which is the point of a primitive that takes a bare polyline.
